newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: UN sanctions panel hopes for Iraq oil sales in Aug.
newsitem.headline: UN sanctions panel hopes for Iraq oil sales in Aug.

text.p: The head of the U.N. sanctions panel on Iraq hopes renewed oil sales will start in the first week of August, once U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan receives and approves an aid distribution plan.
Western diplomats said sanctions panel chairman, Portugal's ambassador Antonio Monteiro, expected Annan to receive the aid distribution plan on Monday.
It was then expected to take around one week for Annan and other U.N. officials to review and approve the plan, setting the stage for Iraq to submit a new pricing formula for renewed oil sales.
"Hopefully, the distribution plan will be presented to the U.N. on Monday. We are looking for Iraqi oil exports the first week of August," a Western diplomat said.
Iraq is allowed to sell $2 billion worth of crude over 180 days in order to buy humanitarian aid for civilians suffering from sanctions imposed on Baghdad after the invasion of Kuwait in 1990.
